clue.text: State representative abused the charming little girl

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York State
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

indicators.note: abused suggests something mistreated and knocked out of shape, so the letters of 'the' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A state representative has mistreated a sweet little girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representative' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it only supplies the parliamentary abbreviation; 'abused' signals the rearranged article.
explanation.definitionFit: A nymphet is a sexually precocious young girl, the meaning popularised by Nabokov's Lolita.

clue.text: American uncle first represented the centre

indicators.note: represented is read as re-presented, presented again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An American uncle was the first to be portrayed at the heart of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' only tells you to put UNCLE ahead of US; 'represented' then rearranges UNCLEUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the central core around which something is built, as in the nucleus of an atom or cell.

clue.text: It strikes over-40s about 1pm, turning up with a purpose

indicators.note: about signals the letters being turned around and rearranged

parts.note: 1pm read as 'one pm', spelt out as letters
a use is a purpose or function

explanation.surface: Something strikes the middle-aged around lunchtime, appearing with intent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up with' is linking surface. The definition is a cryptic description of the change of life that comes to women in middle age.
explanation.definitionFit: The change of life typically arrives for women in their forties or fifties, so it is something that befalls the over-40s.

clue.text: King showing affection to his daughter is widely seen as a warmonger

parts.note: Henry is the name of eight English kings
kissing someone shows affection to them
the king's daughter is Elizabeth I, whose royal cipher is ER (Elizabeth Regina)

explanation.surface: A king fond of his daughter is widely regarded as a warmonger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his daughter' depends on the king being Henry VIII, father of Elizabeth I, whose royal monogram is ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The US Secretary of State during the Vietnam and Cambodia bombings is regarded by critics as a hawk who promoted war.

clue.text: Writer who is poor at reading

indicators.note: poor suggests something done badly, so the letters of 'at reading' are jumbled

explanation.surface: A writer who reads aloud badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who is' is linking; 'poor' rearranges AT READING.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is a writer of tragedies (or an actor who plays them), so a kind of dramatic author.

clue.text: Estate needs management, getting setter in

indicators.note: in, with 'getting' before it, says the setter's word goes inside
management suggests handling and arranging things, so the letters of 'needs' are reordered

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves, so 'setter' gives ME

explanation.surface: An estate requires management, so the puzzle compiler steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting ... in' is split by the setter's word; the reshuffled letters of 'needs' open around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land attached to a manor and kept by its owner, an estate.

clue.text: A drop of the hard stuff before 4's work

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky or other spirits
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nip of whisky before the playwright's performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'A dram' but the letters run DRAM then A. '4' is TRAGEDIAN, a writer of drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama is the body of work produced by a writer of tragedies and other plays.

clue.text: Relative to chemical processes encountered by a mixture of oil in ancient times

parts.note: met is the past tense of meet, to encounter

indicators.note: in places the mixed letters inside the abbreviation for ancient times

parts.note: BC, before Christ, labels dates in ancient times

indicators.note: a mixture stirs things together, so the letters of 'oil' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something met in antiquity is a blend of oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link; the rearranged oil sits between the two letters for ancient times.
explanation.definitionFit: Metabolic describes the body's chemical processes that convert food into energy and tissue.

clue.text: Dame of 5 shattered by dislike when needle's inserted

indicators.note: inserted signals one piece put inside another
shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters of 'by dislike' are rearranged

parts.note: a thorn is a sharp natural needle

explanation.surface: A theatrical dame broken by hostility when a needle is stuck into her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link and '5' is DRAMA; the thorn goes between the forename and the rest of the surname in the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: She was a celebrated English stage actress, made a Dame for her services to the theatre.

clue.text: Small type turns out to be mere lad

indicators.note: turns out suggests one thing being changed into another, so the letters of 'mere lad' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A little sort of person proves to be merely a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small type' looks like a description of a lad, but it is the old printers' name for a small type size.
explanation.definitionFit: In traditional printing, emerald was the name of a small type size, between nonpareil and minion.

clue.text: One of the 19 can get on in the hierarchy

explanation.surface: A clergyman may rise up through the church ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' is CLOTH, the clergy as a body. 'get' and 'in the hierarchy' are linking surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of the clergy attached to a cathedral, so one of those in holy orders.

clue.text: Flexible girl fit to enter training

indicators.note: to enter signals one piece going inside another

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
able means fit or capable
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A supple young woman is fit enough to begin her training.
explanation.walkthrough: The wording suggests the fit word entering training, but it is the training abbreviation that goes between the girl and the fit word.
explanation.definitionFit: Adaptable means able to adjust to new conditions, which is being flexible.

clue.text: Shape Emmy displays is breathtaking

definitions.note: an adjective in the clue for a noun: the disease literally takes one's breath

indicators.note: displays suggests laying things out in a new show, so the letters of 'Shape Emmy' are rearranged

explanation.surface: The figure an Emmy statuette shows is stunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breathtaking' in its usual sense means stunning; here it is taken literally, for a disease that leaves sufferers short of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphysema is a lung disease that damages the air sacs and causes breathlessness, so it literally takes the breath.

clue.text: Would say the reverse of a thick slice

indicators.note: the reverse of means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a slab is a thick flat piece or slice

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what the opposite of a hefty slice would be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Would say' is a sound pun: read it as 'wood, say', a wood for example. A SLAB read backwards gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light wood used for models, so it is an example of a wood.

clue.text: Bogged down a bit in Germany

definitions.meaning: unable to move or make progress
the German noun for a piece or bit, spelt with an umlaut there

explanation.definitionFit: The English word means unable to move on, while the German Stück means a piece.

clue.text: See 3
Like live wires without one being defamed

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the defamed word goes around

parts.note: to defame someone is to insult them
A means one, as in 'a dog'

explanation.surface: Like energetic people being slandered without exception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old meaning 'outside': INSULTED goes around A. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Live electrical wires are wrapped in a non-conducting coating so they are safe to handle.

clue.text: Cecil's apt to become suspicious

indicators.note: to become signals one thing changing into another, so the letters of 'Cecil's apt' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cecil tends to grow distrustful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sceptical means doubting claims, which is to be suspicious of them.

clue.text: See 7
A gong is an establishment expression of respect

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or honour, such as the OBE (Order of the British Empire)
taken as written
taken as written
the established church in England is the Church of England, CE

explanation.surface: Receiving an honour is a sign of the Establishment's esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'gong' is British slang for an honour or decoration, here the OBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a bow or other gesture showing deference and respect.

clue.text: Where water goes, but not in autumn …

parts.note: not in means out
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Water flows away, though not during the autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfall is the mouth of a drain or river where water discharges.

clue.text: What many are reluctant to wear

definitions.text: What many are reluctant to wear

parts.words: What many are reluctant to wear
parts.note: reads like a garment few like to put on; it means the clergy's dress, as in taking holy orders, which few choose

explanation.definitionFit: The cloth means the clergy, whose clerical dress few people are willing to adopt by taking holy orders.

clue.text: … whence it comes, from unknown right hand

indicators.note: from is read as 'made from', so the letters are rearranged into a new word

parts.note: y is a mathematical unknown
taken as written

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue, water comes from an unknown right hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 18 down: water goes to an outfall and comes from this. 'from' rearranges Y, RT and HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire hydrant is a street outlet from which water is drawn from the mains.

clue.text: Stair exercises pedal parts

indicators.note: exercises suggests putting something through its paces, so the letters of 'Stair' are moved around

explanation.surface: Climbing stairs works the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the bones of the ankle and foot, so parts of the foot, pedal meaning of the feet.

clue.text: Practicality is lacking in this land

indicators.note: lacking means doing without, so the word 'is' is taken out

parts.note: realism is a practical, down-to-earth outlook

explanation.surface: This country has no common sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is lacking' removes IS from REALISM; 'in this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or land.

clue.text: Not qualified for display in nude art

indicators.note: putting things on display arranges them for show, so the letters of 'in nude art' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Not trained for appearing in nude art.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrained means lacking the training needed, so not qualified.

clue.text: Retract one in 28, for example

parts.note: 28 is LORIENT, in France, and the French for one is un
say is used to introduce an example

explanation.surface: Withdraw a single example, as one might in a French port.
explanation.walkthrough: '28' is LORIENT, a French port, so 'one' is given in French.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsay something is to take back what one has said, to retract it.

clue.text: Exponent of 5 in current eminence

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a tor is a rocky hill, an eminence

explanation.surface: A performer of plays achieves current fame.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' is DRAMA; an exponent is one who performs it. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor performs drama, so he is an exponent of it.

clue.text: Say Turner turns endlessly ill, provide a painkiller

indicators.note: turns reverses the letters of the preceding pair

parts.note: e.g. means for example, 'say'
Lana Turner was an American film actress

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter

parts.note: sick means ill

explanation.surface: An artist's turns of illness call for something to ease pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter; it is the actress Lana Turner. 'turns' reverses EGLANA to ANALGE; 'endlessly' cuts SICK to SIC. 'provide a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic is a drug that relieves pain.

clue.text: Where flame trees are smash hit on borders of Kenya

indicators.note: smash means to break up, so the letters of 'hit' are rearranged
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A smash hit set on the edges of Kenya.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smash hit' reads as a big success; 'smash' rearranges HIT to THI. Elspeth Huxley's memoir The Flame Trees of Thika is set there.
explanation.definitionFit: This Kenyan town is famous from Elspeth Huxley's memoir about its flame trees.

clue.text: It keeps its mouth open to strike victim

parts.note: to lam is to beat or strike
prey is a victim

explanation.surface: A predator holds its jaws open to attack its victim.
explanation.definitionFit: This jawless fish has a round sucker mouth that stays open to fasten on to its prey.

clue.text: In France, the east is in the west

definitions.text: In France, the east is in the west

parts.words: In France, the east is in the west
parts.note: in French the words for 'the east' name a port in western France, Brittany

explanation.definitionFit: This port's name means the Orient in French, yet it lies on the Breton coast in the west of France.
